results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

result.actual_text:
Dưới đây là hàm Python tính số Fibonacci bằng phương pháp đệ quy (recursion):

### 1. Phân bản đệ quy cơ bản

```python
def fibonacci(n):
    # Trường hợp cơ sở (Base cases)
    if n <= 0:
        return 0
    elif n == 1:
        return 1
    
    # Bước đệ quy (Recursive call)
    return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)

# Ví dụ sử dụng:
n = 10
print(f"Số Fibonacci thứ {n} là: {fibonacci(n)}")
# Output: Số Fibonacci thứ 10 là: 55
```

---

### 2. Phiên bản tối ưu với Memoization (`functools.lru_cache`)

Cách tính đệ quy thuần ở trên có độ phức tạp thời gian là $O(2^n)$ (nhiều tính toán bị lặp lại). Để tối ưu, bạn có thể sử dụng decorator `@lru_cache` để lưu trữ kết quả của các bước đệ quy trước đó:

```python
from functools import lru_cache

@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def fibonacci_memo(n):
    if n <= 0:
        return 0
    elif n == 1:
        return 1
    return fibonacci_memo(n - 1) + fibonacci_memo(n - 2)

# Ví dụ sử dụng với số lớn:
print(fibonacci_memo(100)) 
# Output: 354224848179261915075
```

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary: Goldberg, who was recently inducted into the National Academy of Engineering, is presenting the new approach and results from months of testing this week at the Conference on Robot Learning. He and his team are also releasing open-source code for other roboticists to experiment with, built on NVIDIA’s Isaac open simulation framework  for developers, as well as an industry-standard benchmark for evaluating the performance of robots across industrial tasks. [...] Earlier this year, he and his team began experimenting with a change to the way the robot code is organized. Using a framework they called Graph-as-Policy, robot tasks are segmented into individual skills, such as finding an object, planning a grasp and moving the gripper without collisions. Goldberg likened it to individual building blocks that fit together into something much larger. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet.

items.title: Kenwood High School JROTC Robotics Program earns regional recognition - ClarksvilleNow.com
items.summary: During the current robotics’ competition season, Team 26163X captured first place at the Tennessee State Fair Robotics Competition. The team followed that performance with another first-place finish at a competition in Elizabethton, Tennessee, where it also received a technical award recognizing excellence in robot design and engineering. [...] The teams are scheduled to compete in the V5RC Arsenal Tech Fall Tournament in Fort Wayne, Indiana, and later at the Louisville Slugger Signature Competition, an event expected to attract top robotics programs from across the United States and several international teams. Cadets involved in the program say the experience extends beyond competition. “Robotics has taught us how to work together under pressure and find solutions when things don’t go as planned,” said a member of Team 26163X.”Every [...] CLARKSVILLE TN – The Kenwood High School JROTC Robotics Program has grown from a single robotics team into a four-team program that is competing successfully at regional and national-level events. The program currently fields Teams 26163X, 26163A, 26163L, and 26163S, providing students with opportunities to develop skills in engineering, programming, and problem-solving.

items.title: FDA seeks input on telesurgery, autonomous robotics
items.summary: The FDA is asking the robotics community to submit comments on the discussion paper by Jan. 5. Ahead of that deadline, a public workshop to discuss the topics raised in the paper is scheduled for Dec. 2-3. [...] Under an investigational device exemption from the FDA, Dr. Vipul Patel, founder and medical director of the Global Robotics Institute at AdventHealth Celebration in Florida, in October performed a robotic prostatectomy on a patient about 35 miles away. Last year, Patel completed a transatlantic prostatectomy, operating from Florida on a patient in Angola. [...] The Food and Drug Administration on Friday issued a discussion paper on robotic medical devices with autonomous or remote teleoperation capabilities and is requesting feedback on the systems’ benefits and risks.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: Accelerating engineering for the physical world | OpenAI
items.summary: Today, we’re sharing advances in how OpenAI models help engineers design, simulate, and build physical products. These capabilities span mechanical and electrical engineering and end-to-end system design, and are already helping our internal teams test ideas and iterate faster. [...] of the ability of AI models to positively impact iteration speed for professional workflows. [...] We’re expanding our collaboration with Chip Ganassi Racing (CGR) to explore how OpenAI models can accelerate engineering and prototyping. Working with its R&D team, we’re testing workflows that turn 3D scans of existing parts into editable CAD models and 2D manufacturing drawings. This is particularly useful when the original design files are unavailable.

items.title: Setting a new standard for responsible AI infrastructure | OpenAI
items.summary: The promise of AI is that it gives people more power to shape their own futures. It can help someone learn a new skill, build a business, or solve a problem that was previously out of reach. Building more computing infrastructure capacity in the United States can help lower the cost of delivering AI, put these tools in more people’s hands, and ensure America stays at the forefront of the technology. [...] protect residents, and ensure that the benefits of AI infrastructure are broadly shared. [...] Create opportunities for local workers and businesses.We’ll publish the jobs we expect to create, work with unions and training providers to help residents prepare for them, and report annually on hiring and apprenticeships. We’ll also make sustained investments in priorities residents help select.
